factor_audit.name: Governance and stewardship
material_facts: Unresolved tax assessment and balances-confirmation EOM require a material governance discount.
Parent control, related-party asset purchase and unexplained IPO fee reconciliation weaken minority assurance.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: The audit is unmodified, balances selected for external confirmation and tax cases are appealed; none establishes fraud by itself.
factor_audit.explanation: Weak but not proven disqualifying conduct. G1 Hold rather than unsupported Fail.

factor_audit.name: Competitive advantage
material_facts: Top 10 customers 71.29% of FY25 sales and suppliers 66.33% leave counterparty bargaining power.
Online revenue below 1% and no proven exclusivity, retention cohorts or price premium.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Sourcing breadth, fabric assortment, supplier relationships and growing retail channel are useful practical capabilities.
factor_audit.explanation: Distribution competence is not a demonstrated durable network effect.

factor_audit.name: Demonstrated revenue growth
material_facts: Pre selected FY23–26 reported revenue CAGR11.35% fits 10–15% anchor 6.
FY24 contracted 2.64%, FY25 grew 18.11%, FY26 grew 20.06%; current annual addition 23.18 crore.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: FY22–26 CAGR 41.02% captures a very low early base, not a comparable five-year trend; physical volume/price split remains unavailable.
factor_audit.explanation: No trajectory upgrade without sufficient comparable recent halves/quarters. FY26 newly formed subsidiary has nil revenue, so no acquisition revenue uplift.

factor_audit.name: Accessible growth duration
material_facts: Retail B2C and outsourced processing provide adjacent expansion options.
IPO store budgets provide a tangible route to greater distribution.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Demand access is purchase-order-based, customer concentration high, new stores delayed and unit economics unverified.
factor_audit.explanation: Plausible runway, no proven long protected duration.

factor_audit.name: Incremental capital efficiency
material_facts: Accounting incremental return is distorted by margin expansion and large receivable/advance movements.
No attributable cash contribution/payback for new stores, website investment or outsourced manufacturing.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Three-year gross accounting incremental NOPAT/IC proxy 27.24% is favorable arithmetic, but cannot establish excess project returns.
factor_audit.explanation: NS: current ROCE or aggregate accounting growth cannot substitute for attributable incremental economics.

factor_audit.name: Operating cash realization
material_facts: Reported FY24–26 CFO/PAT ratio of sums−0.98 and FY25 CFO/PAT only 0.27.
Even after removing treasury and capital-advance classification effects, FY26 adjusted CFO −23.04 crore remains strongly negative.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: FY24 and FY25 reported CFO are positive, and part of FY26 outflow is fixed-deposit parking rather than consumed cash.
factor_audit.explanation: Persistent poor realization beyond a merely evidenced transient expansion; GQS cap 5 applies but incomplete point remains NS.

factor_audit.name: Funding resilience
material_facts: Current demand-debt, covenants and unrestricted cash are not verified as of October.
Earmarked IPO cash cannot all be freely netted against debt; remaining projects 17.88 crore exceed 15.1483 restricted cash.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: March balance sheet and June monitor evidence substantial financial assets; conditional base/bull fund themselves.
factor_audit.explanation: NS, not insolvency: historical deposits and hypothetical cash generation do not establish current available funding.

factor_audit.name: Delivery and adaptation
material_facts: FY26 sales 20.06%/PAT51.12% grew but missed earlier stated 30%/60% ambitions.
Original FY26 store deployment slipped into FY27; Gurugram closure generated asset write-off.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Delhi store August 2026 and higher sales demonstrate actual progress, and timing delays have stated operational explanations.
factor_audit.explanation: Delivery is mixed and recent public-market history short; no credit for all six stores as completed.

factor_audit.name: Quality of profit growth
material_facts: Other income 0.5555 crore is only a small portion of FY26 PAT; operating margin expansion drives growth.
Current-share owner EPS 10.19 versus FY25 same-share 6.74 shows growth despite IPO dilution.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Revenue recognition/collection, margin durability and cash conversion are unsettled; weighted EPS growth is materially slower than headline PAT.
factor_audit.explanation: Real reported operating improvement with material realization and normalization uncertainty.

factor_audit.name: Prospective return
material_facts: Ordinary returns cannot be grounded in verified current financing or sustainable incremental economics.
Bear breaches minimum cash; unfinanced terminal arithmetic is not a surviving-investor return.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Conditional base 20.64% and bull 39.24% exceed 15% in explicit funded hypothetical ledgers.
factor_audit.explanation: NS: do not promote conditional arithmetic into an ordinary forecast.

factor_audit.name: Downside resilience
material_facts: Customer/collection stress plus demand-debt repayment and disputed taxes breaches cash in FY27.
Receivables, inventories and capital advances can suffer recovery haircuts; promoter collateral is not investor surplus value.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Reported equity 87.82 crore and historically confirmed FD s offer a buffer if realizable and available.
factor_audit.explanation: Permanent-loss risk material; rescue is separate, dilutive and not available by assumption.

factor_audit.name: Price-implied expectations
material_facts: Low reported PE is not enough to establish normalized collected earnings.
Reverse model needs only 5.37% constant growth under base margins/collections, but those inputs lack verification.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Current-share PE 8.93 and conditional base hurdle entry 115.63 suggest favorable possible pricing, not a demonstrably expensive stock.
factor_audit.explanation: NS: directional cheapness is acknowledged while unreliable normalized economics prevent a defensible expectations score.

factor_audit.name: Executable liquidity
material_facts: Only 16 of 20 and 51 of 60 required common sessions have BSE secondary observations.
Recent observed 5% participation gives zero whole-lot capacity; median observed volume 4200 shares is just 3.5 lots.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: There are occasional larger-volume observations and the dated master indicates eligible SM with 1200-share lot.
factor_audit.explanation: NS because full-session trading/zero-count and executable depth are unverified; missing NSE rows are not BSE zero trades.

sections.title: Identity, Research Setup & Gates
sections.text:
Identity is verified against final prospectus, annual report, BSE listing notice and the 19 October 2026 interoperable master: Game Changers Texfab Limited, BSE SME 544594, TRADEUNO, ISIN INE1GUJ01014. The current CIN is L14101DL2015PLC278723 ; the prospectus has its prelisting U-prefix. Incorporated 6 April 2015 and converted to public limited 2 December 2024, the issuer listed 4 November 2025 after a wholly fresh 53,76,000-share ₹102 IPO. Face value ₹10. There is no OFS to mistake for company proceeds.

The information cutoff is 20 October 2026 and the price observation 19 October 2026 is a secondary historical close, not live executable market depth. Nominal investor horizon is exactly five years to 19 October 2031 with 15% pretax nominal INR equity hurdle. A ₹5 lakh reference position is not a possible exact lot quantity: floor 4 lots/4,800 shares cost ₹436,800 and ceiling 5 lots/6,000 shares cost ₹546,000. There is no portfolio suitability assessment.

FY22–25 historicals are standalone/restated; FY26 is the first consolidated year after an 80%-owned subsidiary incorporated 18 February 2026 with nil revenue. Parent adopted Ind AS effective 1 April 2024. This scope transition is disclosed, not presented as purchased growth. Financial extraction confidence is high for reproduced totals but economic/reliability confidence is low to medium. Current funding, attributable incremental returns and liquidity are low confidence. G1 integrity, G2 financial reliability, G3 funding and G4 implementability are each Hold, unresolved, not conclusively Fail. A G3 Hold alone does not erase business quality; here BQS/GQS are independently incomplete because of CAP/BAL evidence.

sections.title: Scorecard & Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors are GOV 4, MOAT 4, REV 6, DUR 5, CAP NS, CASH 3, BAL NS, EXEC 4, EARN 6, R NS, D 3, P NS and L NS. Every factor has distinct material evidence, a contrary fact and a confidence ceiling in the embedded audit. Missing values never become 5, zero or a peer average. Decimal calculations use exact stated weights, with conventional half-up display only after calculation.

BQS known contribution 3.44 and 80% coverage produce a mathematical missing-factor interval 3.64–5.44. GQS known contribution 4.60 and 85% coverage produce 4.75–6.10 before the persistent CASH 3 override; cap-adjusted range 4.75–5.00, but the point remains NS. IAS has only D 3 contributing 0.60 at 20% coverage; with Q=BQS unavailable alongside R/P/L, its unconstrained missing interval is 1.40–8.60. This interval is uncertainty arithmetic, not a confidence interval or an investable score. The GQS cash ceiling does not create a numeric NS replacement. No governance≤3 override, conclusive G1 Fail or G3 Fail is asserted.

Weights remain exactly the v3.0 framework. BQS uses GOV/MOAT 20% each, REV 12%, DUR 10%, CAP 12%, CASH 10%, BAL/EXEC 8% each; GQS uses REV 40%, DUR 20%, EARN/CAP 15% each and CASH 10%; IAS uses unrounded BQS 25%, R 35%, D 20%, P/L 10% each. All three ranking flags are false; place this issuer in Pending evidence, not the ranked bottom or an Excluded-by-failure bucket.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
TradeUNO sources fabrics across an issuer-described 500-plus suppliers, 22 sourcing zones and 10 sourcing offices and sells primarily through B2B relationships, showrooms and retail channels. It carries fashion, furnishing and technical fabrics, with apparel/customization activity and the FallinLove label. Its outsourced/deemed-manufacturing model means fabric processing can be contracted rather than owned; that avoids some factory investment but does not remove inventory, advances, receivables or customer-credit risk. It is not an asset-free software marketplace merely because a web platform exists.

FY25 fabric revenue ₹113.4076 crore split approximately ₹98.3843 crore B2B and ₹15.0233 crore B2C. Commission ₹1.9891 crore and small made-to-measure activity complete the operating revenue. FY26 statutory categories include ₹116.5113 crore non-deemed fabric revenue and ₹22.1566 crore deemed manufacturing, plus minor made-to-measure, commission and membership amounts. The investor presentation instead classifies total revenue ₹119.9080 crore B2B and ₹18.8386 crore B2C. Those channel numbers sum approximately to group revenue, while statutory fabric categories exclude ₹.0787 crore of other activities; the labels are not interchangeable.

Online FY26 revenue ₹.9690 crore is below 1% of total; most transactions remain offline. Membership ₹.0396 crore is not evidence of a scalable SaaS subscription franchise. FY26 statutory revenue is entirely India; an August 2026 France-order announcement is a prospective business update, not verified recognized export revenue or collected cash. FY25 Haryana represented 72.75% of sales, Delhi 12.99% and UP 9.65%. Cash collection from a concentrated customer base, supplier terms and merchandise mix are more consequential than website visitor counts.

sections.title: Moat & Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible advantage is a combination of fabric assortment, sourcing relationships, fast sample/fulfilment capability and useful offline retail presence. A customer could prefer one supplier that assembles diverse fabrics and coordinates outsourced processing. To deserve a high moat score this must translate into durable retention, pricing power, lower cost-to-serve or exclusivity after credit losses and working-capital costs. None of those is quantified well enough here. Customer relationships are generally based on purchase orders rather than assured long-term take-or-pay contracts.

FY25 top customer 14.74%, top five 47.12% and top ten 71.29% of revenue create meaningful bargaining and renewal risk. Supplier top five 42.25% and top ten 66.33% also constrain bargaining; the June 2025 quarter was more concentrated, with top 10 suppliers 92%. FY26 Note 52 says four customers individually exceed 10% but aggregate 39.77%; these cannot both hold literally. Rather than invent a correction or use the lower number to award diversification, the prior certified concentration table is retained with a current gap. Retail growth could diversify, but requires store unit economics and cash collection evidence.

Peers are directional business checks, not interchangeable valuations. T T Limited’s FY25 report shows restructuring from spinning and a large exceptional item; its headline profit multiple is not a clean recurring fabric benchmark. Bhandari Hosiery integrates knitting/dyeing/finishing/garmenting, so factory economics differ from TradeUNO’s sourcing model. Arvind has substantially broader textile and advanced-materials manufacturing and scale. The prospectus’s historical T T/Bhandari PEs use old price/EPS dates and are not updated into a fictitious October 2026 peer basket. Fragmented supply, buyer switching, raw material/pass-through prices and fashion obsolescence explain a MOAT 4 rather than a network-effect rating.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Five annual revenue observations are FY22 ₹35.0788 crore, FY23 ₹100.4971 crore, FY24 ₹97.8438 crore, FY25 ₹115.5631 crore and FY26 ₹138.7465 crore. Four observations FY23–26 support a three-year CAGR of 11.35% with positive comparable endpoints. This window is selected before scoring because no six-observation five-year comparable series was recovered. Five/ten-year CAGR fields stay null. FY22–26 four-year CAGR 41.02% is shown for context, not mislabeled a five-year CAGR; the FY22 starting scale produces a misleadingly exciting headline relative to the subsequent flat FY24.

Annual additions FY23–26 are ₹65.4183 crore,−₹2.6533 crore, ₹17.7193 crore and ₹23.1834 crore. Growth moved from −2.64% in FY24 to 18.11% in FY25 and 20.06% in FY26. No verified current FY27 comparable interim/TTM pair was recovered by cutoff, so no further trajectory bonus is applied. The archived H1 FY26 filing is an earlier period, not current FY27 data. REV starts 6 for 10–15% CAGR and stays 6; sustained comparable halves/quarters would be needed for a documented net+1 adjustment.

Retail B2C fabric revenue increased from ₹2.6714 crore FY23 to ₹4.8527 crore FY24 and ₹15.0233 crore FY25, providing a real mix shift. It does not demonstrate unit volume growth, same-store growth or price power without physical-volume and collection data. Technical fabric revenue fell from ₹11.9234 crore FY23 to ₹1.1461 crore FY24 before ₹2.9241 crore FY25; that is not uninterrupted technical-textile acceleration. Online FY26 ₹.9690 crore is higher than FY25 ₹.9075 crore but below FY24 ₹1.4246 crore. A presentation‘acceleration’ label cannot reverse that arithmetic. Acquisition growth is not inserted: the new subsidiary had nil revenue in FY26.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The bottom-up opportunity is additional showrooms, more customer fabric categories and outsourced processing tied to existing B2B demand, rather than a national textile TAM allocation. The original IPO capex plan envisaged six roughly 8,000-square-foot stores in Chandigarh, Lucknow, Noida, Ahmedabad, Delhi and Pune. Budget ₹15 crore IPO capex plus a small internal contribution was supposed to deploy in FY26. By March and June 2026 only ₹2.79 crore of IPO capex had been used; remaining ₹12.21 crore moved into FY27. The August Delhi 10,000-square-foot opening is evidence of progress, not evidence that six stores are open or all have positive payback.

Remaining capex ₹12.21 crore, WC ₹.68 crore and GCP ₹4.99 crore total ₹17.88 crore against ₹15.1483 crore earmarked unspent cash, leaving ₹2.7317 crore to fund from other resources under the disclosed allocation. GCP includes potential unidentified acquisitions; the model spends it once without inventing acquired profit or terminal surplus property. Ordinary capex and IPO-project floors overlap: the model uses the higher of normal capex or annual project floor rather than adding the same investment twice. Opening capital advances ₹2.4022 crore remain assets and are not paid again. No future warrant receipt is manufactured; no outstanding options/reserved shares are disclosed in FY26.

FY23–26 aggregate incremental NOPAT/closing operating capital proxy is 27.24%, but cash realization and capital allocation are not attributable at project level. It is not a CAP score. FY25 website purchase from parent ₹1.4448683 crore, capital advances, new/closed leases and sharply changing margin create attribution problems. Required upgrades are store cohorts with sales, collected gross margin, operating rent, inventory, receivables, full fit-out/capital advances and contribution after central cost. Until then CAP NS, GQS NS and its CASH 3 ceiling remain. Duration 5 reflects accessible opportunity with concentration and execution constraints, not a forecast that all funded capacity will sell.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Force Multiplier Ecommerce holds 12,349,597 shares, about 69.02%, and the promoters control the issuer. The holding-company website asset transaction and other family/related-party sales, purchases and advances require arm’s-length scrutiny. FY26 related party loans ₹4.25 crore were both received and repaid; zero ending balance must not conceal that gross financing activity. Related-party transactions table totals combine commercial transactions and loans, so its ₹8.5134 crore aggregate is not treated as an 8.5134 crore sales dependency. Promoter-firm property pledged to bank is collateral, not an asset minority shareholders own.

Auditor transitions in 2024 include resignations citing preoccupation. The record does not establish concealed misconduct as their cause. The current audit is unmodified, but emphasizes balances subject to confirmation/reconciliation and unprovided tax/GST disputes. The tax authority assessment alleged non-genuine purchases and share premium transactions; the company appealed and management believes a favorable outcome likely based on advisers. This is an unresolved assessment/appeal, not a final judicial finding of fraud. The GST underlying disputed tax was paid earlier and the prospectus describes appeal against penalty; the model does not pay both again. The FY26 annual report lists three criminal cases filed by the company, not three charges against management; the prospectus details one cheque-recovery complaint. No speculative legal recovery is valued.

Promises-versus-delivery: the December 2025 call stated approximately 30% FY26 sales and 60% profit growth ambitions; audited FY26 achieved 20.06% and 51.12%. The original FY26 store timeline slipped to FY27 in monitoring reports, with management citing operational/practical considerations. Delhi’s August 2026 opening is a positive milestone, while FY26 Gurugram closure/relocation included ₹.4077 crore asset write-off. IPO issue fees are another open execution/control question: ₹8.21 crore utilized against ₹5.48 crore estimated, but only ₹6.2695 crore charged to premium. The ₹1.9405 crore gap is preserved, not explained speculatively as tax, timing or reimbursement. Lock-ins for 4,449,134 shares end 20 November 2026, with further tranches in 2027/2028; potential additional float is not a claim that promoters will sell.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY26 EBITDA excluding other income is ₹27.0387 crore and EBIT ₹25.6720 crore, versus ₹18.5917/₹17.5708 crore in FY25. Gross value added proxy, revenue less materials consumed, expands sharply; it is not an audited product gross margin because commission/mix and service cost classification differ. PAT ₹18.2325 crore, owner PAT ₹18.2331 crore and weighted EPS ₹12.42 are not interchangeable. Current 17.892814 million-share owner EPS is ₹10.1902. No share bonus wealth creation is implied: FY25 included a 400:1 bonus; original FY22 EPS is not directly comparable to today's capital.

Reported CFO FY22–26 is −₹.4142 crore,−₹1.8351 crore, ₹2.5535 crore, ₹3.2660 crore and −₹39.8497 crore. Reported cash capex is ₹.0250 crore, ₹.0374 crore, ₹.6605 crore, ₹1.5795 crore and ₹3.3534 crore. FY24–26 CFO/PAT ratio of sums is -0.98, not an average of annual ratios; cumulative reported FCF −₹39.62 crore. Investment in completed assets is not an explanation of weak CFO, while deposit classification is specifically reconciled. FY26 pre-WC operating cash ₹27.3219 crore less ₹60.8022 crore net working capital/classification movement gives −₹33.4803 crore before the reported ₹6.3694 crore tax line.

The ₹15 crore FD principal and ₹.3306 crore accrued FD interest sit in other current financial assets and are included in the operating outflow. Moving those treasury items and ₹1.4816 crore capital advance increase out of CFO yields analytical CFO −₹23.0375 crore; adjusted cash capex ₹4.8350 crore produces FCF −₹27.8725 crore. Moving cash flow classification does not create cash. The ₹.3306 crore accrued interest is not opening cash or a second future income claim. The tax cash line closely matches tax expense while net current tax liability also changes; without payment support it remains source-reported, not arbitrarily‘corrected’. Future model pays opening tax liability ₹.9823 crore once in addition to future current tax.

Trade receivables ₹48.9605 crore increased ₹22.32 crore, inventories ₹19.7443 crore increased ₹3.4693 crore, trade payables fell ₹10.5512 crore, and other current assets rose ₹7.7201 crore. Average AR days 99.44 versus 69.22 differ from closing days 128.80 versus 84.15. Net ECL allowance ₹.5737 crore on gross receivables ₹49.5342 crore does not settle recoverability. Audit KAM 1–2-year ageing ₹3.2366 crore conflicts with detailed note ₹.1543 crore; both are cited. The‘zero inventory risk’ retail marketing claim is scoped, not accepted for a group with ₹19.74 crore inventory.

FY26 equity ₹87.8171 crore includes NCI ₹.0194 crore; debt ₹9.0088 crore, lease claims ₹4.3712 crore, cash ₹2.1533 crore, MF ₹5.0525 crore and FD principal ₹15 crore. Financing-based operating capital proxy ₹79.3078 crore reconciles within ₹.0003 crore source-rounding to operating assets minus operating liabilities ₹79.3075 crore. It excludes cash/MF/FD/accrual/DTA and adds back current tax liability; leases and ROU are paired. Forecast operating NWC ₹67.7815 crore excludes capital advances and treasury, includes trade advances/GST/prepayments and deducts non-interest operating liabilities. Historical ROIC and incremental proxies are fully calculated but cannot attribute value creation. Statutory delay interest ₹.5137 crore versus ₹.1676 crore FY25 is recurring control cost, not harmless other income.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹91, current-share FY26 PE is 8.93 times and price/owner book 1.85 times. Dividing price by weighted EPS ₹12.42 wrongly suggests 7.33 times. The primary hybrid EV ₹164.78 crore adds March demand debt and subtracts assumed unrestricted cash/MF ₹7.0575 crore but excludes earmarked IPO ₹15.1483 crore. Cash-lease EBITDA deducts ₹.8599 crore cash rent and gives EV/EBITDA 6.29 times. A separate lease-inclusive alternative is 6.26 times, adding lease claims to EV against pre-rent EBITDA. The models do not subtract lease claims again after cash rent. These are October price/March balance hybrids, not certified current net debt. Reported FCF yield -26.53% is negative; excluding earmarked cash in one EV case and spending it in forecast is explicit, not double counting.

Annual FY27–FY32 cash/debt/WC/tax/capex/shares ledgers start at 31 March 2026; the investor horizon is exactly 19 October 2026–19 October 2031, with October terminal interpolated between FY31/FY32. That bridge does not pretend to know actual April–October movements. Base growth 15/15/12/10/8/8%, cash-lease EBITDA margin 16%, AR days 120→100, inventory 60 days, payables 25 days and normal capex 2% sales are analyst assumptions. Bear growth−20/0/3/5/5/5%, margin 9%, AR 170→140, inventory 90 days, payables 15; bull 25/22/20/18/15/12%, margin 19%, AR 90→75, inventory 50 days, payables 35. Cost ratios, DA, normal cash-tax 25.168%, late-statutory charges and debt interest are explicit. Demand debt is repaid in FY27 with half year interest, not assumed rolled over. Capex floors ₹7/₹5.21 crore and GCP ₹4.99 crore are paid once; restricted cash releases only for model-eligible objects. No new ordinary financing, dividends, warrant receipts or acquisition earnings are assumed. Minimum free cash ₹2 crore is retained and not added as excess cash. Newly formed subsidiary gets no invented future activity; current NCI book claim ₹.0194 crore is reserved.

Terminal cash-lease EBITDA multiples 6/8/10 are explicit normalization assumptions, not purported current peer averages. Base operating EV ₹326.31 crore plus net excess cash ₹89.86 crore less NCI gives ₹416.14 crore hypothetical equity and ₹232.58/share. Base/bull internally funded conditional IRRs are 20.64%/39.24%. Bear funding fails, so its conditional unfinanced IRR is null; its unfunded valuation diagnostic is not a realizable price. Actual current funding unverified means all ordinary IRRs, ordinary terminal prices and ordinary entry fields stay null for every case, including rescue. A terminal DCF cross-check uses 18/16/14% business discounts and 2/4/5% mature growth, ongoing capex and growth WC; these rates are risk ranges, not claimed statistically estimated WACC.

The 15% five-year hurdle needs ₹183.03 terminal price/₹327.50 crore equity. Conditional reverse growth solves approximately 5.37% constant growth under base economics and passes a funded bisection crossing check; it is not an ordinary forecast. Base conditional entry arithmetic ₹115.63 at 15% changes to ₹131.97/₹101.66 at 12%/18%. Entry and exit frictions 1%/3% each lower base conditional IRR to 20.16%/19.20%. Two 3×3 grids rerun margin/collection days and growth/terminal multiple with funding flags. Low valuation is acknowledged, but numerical precision cannot cure unverified cash or collection economics.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest positive case is that margins reflect a better retail/deemed manufacturing mix, IPO capital absorbs working capital growth, receivables collect and store expansion broadens the customer base. With normalizing collections and 16% cash-lease EBITDA margin, the conditional base indeed exceeds 15%; the analysis does not dismiss this because disclosures are imperfect. The strongest negative case is that margins overstate collectible economics, a key customer reduces orders, supplier credit contracts, demand debt is called and tax appeals lose. Inventory recovery and unconfirmed advances then offer less protection than book value implies.

The linked bear contracts FY27 sales by 20%, compresses cash margin to 9%, stretches collections to 170 days and inventory 90 days, repays ₹9.0088 crore demand debt and pays ₹5.5422 crore disputed tax/GST stress once. It breaches ₹2 crore minimum cash in FY27, with peak gap ₹10.29 crore through October 2031. Negative cash is not an authorized borrowing facility. Therefore unfinanced bear IRR and ordinary terminal price stay null, rather than pretending the company survives to a terminal quote. Later FY32 is only an interpolation anchor; funding assessment stops at the actual investor horizon.

A separate rescue illustration issues new shares at ₹45.50, half entry price, with 3% gross issue cost, exactly when modeled cash otherwise breaches ₹2 crore. It raises ₹10.61 crore gross, pays ₹0.32 crore fees and leaves existing owners 88.47% of the modeled capital. Its conditional rescue IRR is -13.47% annually, not the ordinary bear return. No such financing offer is known available. Price recovery, bank enforcement, working capital haircuts and intra-year liquidity could worsen the outcome. Permanent loss risk is material, not an invented bankruptcy probability. The thesis -break variable is collected operating profit after full reinvestment, not just management’s reported margin.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
At unchanged current shares, 5×/10× prices ₹455/₹910 need ₹814.12/₹1628.25 crore equity. Holding base October 2031 net cash and cash-lease EBITDA 16%/8 times constant, required terminal revenue is about ₹565.85/₹1201.88 crore, versus base ₹254.93 crore and bull ₹367.37 crore. These are mechanical requirements, not a TAM-share claim. The bull’s higher 19% margin/10 times multiple and cash generation produce ₹476.21/share, slightly more than 5× entry; that is conditional mathematical feasibility, not proof of a 5× opportunity.

A credible 5× route requires both much greater collected revenue and margin retention, with funded store and working capital expansion and no adverse ownership dilution. A 10× route needs materially more than the declared bull assumptions or multiple expansion. Applying 10× to historical EPS alone hides IPO share count and future capital needs. Any rescue increases required total terminal capitalization for original holders to obtain the same per-share outcome; the stress model does not add new money without issuing new shares. Classification: 5× possible only in aggressively favorable conditional assumptions; 10× unsupported by current evidence, neither assigned a fabricated probability.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Obtain October/current bank balances, restricted/unrestricted FD classification, MF realizability, debt maturity/covenants and committed unused facilities. Baseline March debt ₹9.0088 crore and June unspent IPO ₹15.15 crore; an undrawn limit must be verified, not inferred.
2. Reconcile all IPO objects and issue fees ₹8.21 crore versus ₹6.2695 crore premium charge, including payments/taxes/any prepaid expenses. Require an explanation, not a second fee assumption. Track original ₹15 crore capex budget and ₹2.79 crore used.
3. Reconcile customer ageing ₹3.2366 crore KAM 1–2 years versus ₹.1543 crore Note 17, independent confirmations and subsequent receipts. Track closing AR days 128.80 and average 99.44 separately; further worsening without collection proof is adverse.
4. Resolve FY26 major customer 4× above 10% versus 39.77% aggregate. Obtain top 10 sales/collections and contract renewals, not merely names or assurances.
5. Measure each new store’s open-date, same-store/new-store revenue, cash gross profit, rent, receivables, inventory, advances, capex and payback. Opening Delhi does not complete all six locations.
6. Track CFO/PAT and FCF after treasury reclassification, ECL coverage, inventory ageing and supplier credit. Another negative adjusted CFO year would further weaken the cash thesis.
7. Check tax/GST appeals and payments; distinguish authority assessment, company defense and final order. Monitor late-statutory interest baseline ₹.5137 crore, audit EOM and any new related party deployment.
8. Before implementation, refresh surveillance, 1,200-share lot, current float/encumbrances, bid/ask depth and complete BSE 20/60-session turnover. Note 20 November 2026 lock-in expiry without assuming a sale. No automatic trade or unsolicited recurring monitor is created by this dossier.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold, unresolved / Pending evidence. The business is not rejected merely because it is small or its price is low; it shows genuine reported growth and conditional valuation upside. It is not yet a demonstrated compounder because GOV/MOAT/CASH/EXEC are weak-to-mixed and CAP/BAL unscoreable. BQS/GQS/IAS remain NS; no quality/growth/investment ranking is justified. Four gates remain Hold rather than proven Fail. A price fall alone would not resolve financial reliability, current funding or project returns.

The actual ₹5 lakh implementation test is 4 lots ₹436,800 or 5 lots ₹546,000, not fractional shares. Only 16 of recent 20 and 51 of 60 common exchange sessions have observed secondary BSE prices. Missing dates remain unknown; the absence of the ISIN from NSE issuer history must not be converted to BSE zero trades. Across 16 recent observations, median volume 4,200 shares and median close× volume ₹412,650 look more liquid than a one-lot constraint allows: at 5% participation no observation permits a single 1,200-share lot. At 10%, three observed days permit one each, total 3 lots, less than the 4-lot floor position. The 60-window observed 5% capacity total is 11 lots across 5 observed days, but missing days and live bid depth prevent a reliable future exit estimate. L stays NS, not an invented low point based on incomplete zero counts.

Evidence that could change the conclusion: externally reconciled collection/ageing and IPO-fees, current available funding without unrecognized claims, and attributable cash returns from new stores. With that evidence, the favorable conditional valuation would merit revisiting. Until then conditional base entry arithmetic is not an actionable fair value or buy instruction. No allocation or trade is made.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The canonical JSON embeds all 15 sections, 13 factor audits, four gates, exact Decimal score contributions/bounds, financial-only source inputs, five annual historicals, annual forecast/rescue ledgers, sensitivities, reverse hurdle and dated lot-aware liquidity observations. Sources are linked with document dates, page locators and SHA256 hashes. Issuer-hosted final prospectus and annual report are primary; exchange filings mirrored by Business Standard retain original filing identity. The 19 October quote is secondary. The dated official master confirms identity, issued capital and lot, not current surveillance clearance. Peer descriptions are business comparisons, not independent proof of TradeUNO’s claimed advantage.

Source verification and model reproduction are separate. Source checks compare declared financial inputs and specific inconsistencies against recovered primary tables; they do not confirm private bank/customer balances or resolve audit EOM. Offline isolated reproduction only proves that archived inputs/code can regenerate the published math. Decimal-score/common-schema QA does not certify the issuer or forecast. Every derived summary is regenerated from the final canonical model; ordinary return/entry fields remain null while current funding is unverified.

Unresolved items include October cash/debt, covenants/availability, receivable confirmation/ageing, IPO fees/prepaid-cost classification, customer concentration table, tax payments versus reported cash flow, incremental store/website economics, price-versus volume, same-store performance, minority project allocation, current pledges/surveillance and complete BSE trade history. All forecasts, margins, credit terms, capex minimums, earmarked release, payout policy, tax/interest, terminal multiples/discount rates and rescue offer are analyst assumptions, not company promises. Nominal five-year returns do not account for investor-specific tax.

Privacy-safe compact/full private backups omit raw PDFs, HTML, OCR, images and identifier-bearing regulatory attachments. They retain financial-only extracts, code/results, source URLs/hashes and QA receipts. No individual tax/national identifiers or bank account numbers are intentionally retained. Original documents remain local for verification; the archives are private analytical deliverables, not public source-document redistribution.
